hints: Look carefully at the three names and ask yourself which one describes what happens inside the nucleus when chromosomes first become visible.
Remember that the full cell cycle is much bigger than mitosis, with a long preparation stage before it and cytoplasm splitting after it.
walkthrough:
**Separate cell cycle from mitosis**

Think of the cell cycle as the whole story. It has a long preparation part called interphase, then nuclear division called mitosis, then splitting of the cytoplasm called cytokinesis.

So: cell cycle = interphase + mitosis + cytokinesis

**Check each event in turn**

1 interphase is the stage for growth and DNA replication before division, so it is not part of mitosis. 3 cytokinesis is division of the cytoplasm after the nucleus has divided, so it is also not part of mitosis. 2 prophase is the first stage of nuclear division when chromosomes condense, so it is part of mitosis.

**Pick the matching option**

Only event 2 fits, which matches option D, 2 only.

options.A: Incorrect because it includes interphase and cytokinesis, which are separate from nuclear division.
options.B: Incorrect because although prophase is correct, interphase is preparation for mitosis, not part of it.
options.C: Incorrect because interphase alone is the period of growth and DNA synthesis before mitosis starts.
options.D: Correct because prophase is the first stage of mitosis, while 1 and 3 belong to other parts of the cell cycle.
